description: Updates are opened from the dependency dashboard, so opening a PR stays manual and `automerge` finishes the job. `platformAutomerge` hands the merge to GitHub's native auto-merge, which waits only for required checks: the `check` workflow must stay required on `master` for this to be safe.
`vulnerabilityAlerts` skips dashboard approval, so it keeps a person in front of the merge.

packageRules.description: Constraints are open `>=`, so every release is already in range and the default strategy proposes nothing. `update-lockfile` turns updates into named PRs that touch only `uv.lock`. No soak: `uv lock --upgrade-package` takes no version and resolves to the newest release anyway, so a soak would only make the target and the result disagree.
These change ruff/mypy diagnostics with no source change, so they are kept apart from the runtime group to make new findings attributable to the PR that introduced them.
No mise.lock here, so lock file maintenance would only leave a permanently pending dashboard row. Fallback name for tools added later; python and uv are regrouped by package name below.

mise.toml resolves to `python/cpython` (github-tags) while .python-version is read by the pyenv manager as `python`; matching both names keeps one version in both files. requires-python in pyproject.toml is left to be raised by hand.
mise.toml resolves uv to `astral-sh/uv` (github-releases); `matchPackageNames` matches the package name, not the dep name.
